claims.statement: The UCI engine allows at most one active search; `go`, `ucinewgame` and `quit` first retire (cancel and settle) any active search, so the old search prints its bestmove before a new one starts.

Settling a search is guarded by a lock and a `settled` flag, so exactly one bestmove is printed per `go` regardless of races between the deadline clock, supervisor, stop and new commands; streamed analysis stops once a search is settled.

Search deadlines are None for infinite, ponder, or when neither movetime nor the side-to-move's clock is given; otherwise the engine computes a soft and a hard deadline, each floored at 50 ms and capped at the time left: movetime gives a single deadline of movetime-150, while a clock gives soft = min(remaining/(movestogo or 30)+increment, remaining)-150 and hard = remaining-150.
Cancelled or failed searches still produce a bestmove (System 1's pick or a 0000 forfeit); failures also emit `info string error: <message>` before it.

`go infinite` and `go ponder` searches are held: a finished result is not printed until `stop` or `ponderhit`; `ponderhit` converts the search to a normal one, settling immediately if done or arming a deadline otherwise; stop/ponderhit without an active held search are no-ops.

Completion rows are checked in order: a committed ply of the search's own request wins (even if cancelled), then resignation or other terminal outcome (bestmove 0000 with info reason), then a rejected position (bestmove 0000), then System 1's pick, else a forfeit.

The fallback move is the state's `fallback_move` (System 1's top-ranked move replayed when still allowed) when the latest turn belongs to this request and the move is in the legal pool; otherwise the engine prints `info string forfeits: no move to play` and `bestmove 0000` — it never plays a random move.
`bestmove 0000` is a null move rather than a standard UCI resignation and is intended to be scored as a forfeit by GUIs; fastchess (pinned at v1.8.2-alpha) scores it as an illegal-move loss.

When a fallback is played, the agent's turn remains pending; the GUI's next position includes the fallback, the core lifecycle marks the pending turn abandoned and syncs the fallback in as an external ply.

A game continues on the same thread only if the new position has the same normalized root FEN and its move list extends the checkpointed moves; takebacks, different roots, and `ucinewgame` start a new `uci-<uuid>` thread.
Illegal `searchmoves` are dropped with an info string, but the restriction is never widened: if all are illegal an empty restrict is sent and the agent rejects it with bestmove 0000.

The engine advertises case-insensitive options Config, Model, ReasoningEffort (default/low/medium/high, where default maps to no effort), SystemOneModel, Policy, Threshold (0..1), K (1..255), Memory (a check box accepting true/false and legacy summarize/none), MoveList (both/legal/candidates/none) and Seed (0..2^31-1), not Ponder; invalid or unknown options produce info strings and are ignored.

Option changes are queued during a search and applied after it settles (or at the next go / idle isready); when applied, the agent is rebuilt through the factory with the same checkpointer; isready always answers readyok immediately.

The UCI engine forces draw_claims="never" onto every settings value it builds agents and run configs from (overriding flags, config files or constructor settings), leaving draw adjudication to the GUI; the `uci` command has no draw-claims flag.
`lcchess uci` runs the agent in-process over stdin/stdout with logging on stderr so stdout carries only protocol output; stdin is read in an executor and end of input is treated as quit.
UCI runs are traced as `chess-uci` with tag and metadata surface=uci plus every setting (including draw_claims) and the values actually sent where model_kwargs changed them.

`mise run test:uci` plays two games under fastchess between System 1-only engines with seeds 1 and 2 (st=3, 60-move cap) and passes only if both games have a result and no termination other than normal or adjudication.
The `lcchess uci` command builds its ChessContext from an optional `--config` settings file, then `--reset` names back to defaults, then the flags that were given; `--memory` is a boolean flag.

Queued options are applied one at a time in order; when validation or the agent factory raises for an entry, the engine prints `info string options not applied: <error>` and keeps the previous settings and agent for that entry while still applying the rest (e.g. Memory refused for a model without a known input limit).

Replacing the UCI thread (on ucinewgame or a non-extending position) deletes the old thread from the checkpointer, only while no search is outstanding, so the checkpointer retains only the current game.
All `info string` output is produced by splitting text into one prefixed line per non-blank line, so multi-line agent text or error messages cannot forge UCI commands such as `bestmove` on stdout.

`setoption name Config value <path>` replaces every setting with the loaded settings file (relative to the engine's working directory), later options patch it, and an empty value or `<empty>` restores the settings the engine started with; an unreadable or invalid file is reported as an invalid value and changes nothing.
The engine requires the seed to be within 0..2^31-1 for every settings value it accepts: an out-of-range launch seed fails construction and an out-of-range config seed is not applied.

At the soft deadline the engine cancels the search only if System 1 has already left a usable pick for this search; otherwise it keeps waiting until the hard deadline before cancelling, so a slow move can run past its per-move budget.
